title: Turnip Greens, Frozen, Cooked, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: Turnip greens are the leafy tops of the turnip plant, a nutrient‑dense green vegetable. The frozen, cooked, no‑added‑fat version retains most of the vitamins and minerals while offering a convenient, ready‑to‑use product.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnip greens belong to the Brassicaceae family, which includes broccoli, cabbage, and mustard.
They are rich in glucosinolates, compounds that may support liver detoxification.
In the United States, frozen turnip greens are a common side dish in school cafeterias and fast‑food kitchens.
The raw leaves have a mildly bitter flavor that mellows with cooking.
Turnip greens contain more vitamin K per serving than spinach.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Rich source of vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene in turnip greens converts to vitamin A, supporting vision and immunity.

items.title: Good source of folate
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important during periods of rapid growth.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Minerals: calcium and iron
items.content: Calcium supports bone structure, while iron is vital for oxygen transport.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Turnip greens contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney‑stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Thyroid considerations
items.content: Glucosinolates may affect thyroid function when consumed in very large amounts.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to Brassicaceae greens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frozen cooked turnip greens can be added to soups, stews, salads, omelets, or served as a side dish. They reheat quickly in a skillet with a splash of water or broth.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product at –18 °C in its original packaging. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
